summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Introduced in House):

blocks.text: Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Amendments Act of 2025
This bill revises the water rights settlement agreement entered into by the Crow Tribe of Montana and Montana.

The Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Act of 2010 ratified, authorized, and confirmed the water rights compact between the tribe and Montana. Among other provisions, this settlement act authorized the Bureau of Reclamation to plan, design and construct the following two major projects on the Crow Reservation: (1) the rehabilitation and improvement of the Crow Irrigation Project (CIP); and (2) the planning, design, and construction of the MR&I System (the municipal, rural, and industrial water system of the Crow Reservation).
Among other provisions, the bill revises the settlement act to
replace references to the MR&I System with MR&I Projects;
establish a nontrust, interest-bearing account (to be known as the Crow CIP Implementation Account) to allow Reclamation to continue to work on the rehabilitation of the CIP;
create a new MR&I Projects Account, through which the tribe must use funds for activities related to water production, treatment, or delivery infrastructure; and
extend by five years (to 2030) the period during which the tribe has the exclusive right to construct hydropower facilities on the Yellowtail Afterbay Dam in Montana.

The Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Amendments Act of 2025 changes an earlier water rights agreement between the Crow Tribe of Montana and the state of Montana. That agreement was approved by the Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Act of 2010, which allowed the Bureau of Reclamation to plan, design, and build two major water projects on the Crow Reservation: the rehabilitation and improvement of the Crow Irrigation Project, and a municipal, rural, and industrial water system for the reservation.

The new bill updates that earlier law in several ways. It replaces references to the single water system with references to "MR&I Projects," a broader term covering more than one project. It creates a nontrust, interest-bearing account called the Crow CIP Implementation Account, so the Bureau of Reclamation can keep working on repairing and improving the irrigation project.
The bill also sets up a new MR&I Projects Account. The tribe must use money from this account only for activities related to water production, treatment, or delivery infrastructure.
Finally, the bill extends by five years, to 2030, the period during which the tribe has the exclusive right to build hydropower facilities at the Yellowtail Afterbay Dam in Montana.
